canonical_question: Is the '0–2%' linear thermal strain value a simulation result or a measured value, and how does it justify the 'large number of dislocations'?

question_variants.question: Is the '0–2%' linear thermal strain value a simulation result or a measured value, and how does it justify the 'large number of dislocations'?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text presents the '0-2%' linear thermal strain as a value used to explain the formation of dislocations due to thermal contraction stress, but it does not clarify if this is a measured value or a simulation/calculation result, nor does it provide the mathematical justification linking this specific strain value to the 'large number of dislocations' quantitatively.

answers.answer: The text states that linear thermal strain during cooling is approximately 0–2% and that the resulting thermal contraction stress can form a large number of dislocations. It does not specify whether the 0-2% is a measured or simulated value, nor does it provide the quantitative link between this strain and the dislocation density.
answers.boundary_limitation: Origin (measured vs simulated) and quantitative justification of the strain-dislocation link are not provided.
evidence_spans: SLM-built HEA had a face-centered cubic (FCC) single-phase random solid solution.
In addition, SLM-built HEA was composed of epitaxial growth grains, dislocation network and nano-sized oxides.

Room- and high-temperature compression tests confirmed that SLM-built HEA has outstanding mechanical properties in all temperature ranges compared to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEAs reported up to the present.
